title: The Arazzo catalogue's seven specification extensions
description: `x-veredictum-cite` sits on a workflow, a step or a criterion; a criterion without one inherits its step's, and a step its workflow's. `x-veredictum-check` sits on a criterion only, for the judgements no standard Arazzo criterion can express. `x-veredictum-derive` sits on a step only, and names new step outputs, each one function of BASE OBJECT_VERSION_ID applied to one of the step's own outputs; `validate` also refuses an `of` the step does not declare and a derived name that collides with a declared output. `x-veredictum-principal` sits on a step only, and names the principal the step is sent as instead of the run's ordinary credential; a run whose party supplies no credential for that principal skips every workflow with such a step with the reason `not-declared`. `x-veredictum-scope` sits on a step only, never beside `x-veredictum-principal`, and names the scope set of the access token the step presents; a row whose scope set the party's IXIT covers with no token is skipped with the reason `not-declared`. `x-veredictum-control` sits on a workflow only, and every refusal workflow, one with a criterion `$statusCode == 400` or `$statusCode == 422`, carries one: it names the workflow whose request is the same apart from the one defect, and a refusal row whose control was not accepted in the same run is errored; `validate` refuses a control on any other workflow and one that names no workflow, the workflow itself or another refusal workflow. `x-veredictum-section` sits on a document's `info` only, and names the BASE section of its capability folder that `catalogue/chapters.yaml` declares. `validate` also checks that a citation's quote occurs, after whitespace normalization, inside the named section of the named vendored file, and that the file belongs to no document the release marks RETIRED, which no schema can state. A citation whose source sits under `specs/openehr-development/` rests on development text alone: it is checked against the pinned development snapshot under every profile, carries no `development` wording, and its workflow is skipped with the reason `development-only` under the released profile and counts toward no released coverage.

source.description: The vendored file, relative to the repository root: released text, or, under `specs/openehr-development/`, text only the pinned development snapshot holds.

section.description: A top-level key or a JSON Pointer in a YAML or JSON source; when the element is a number, a boolean or `null`, the quote is that value as JSON text and is matched by value. In a Markdown or AsciiDoc source, the title of exactly one heading, or a path of titles joined by ` > ` in which each heading sits directly under the one before it; a title that matches more than one heading is refused. In an XML Schema (`.xsd`) source, the `name` of one top-level `xs:element`, `xs:complexType` or `xs:simpleType`, optionally after its kind and a space (`complexType COMPOSITION`); the quote is matched in that definition's source text.

quote.description: The sentence that assigns the expectation, copied verbatim.

report.description: The upstream-report issue in this repository that records a defect, contradiction or silence in the cited text.

level.description: The requirement level of the quote: `must` (the default) for MUST, SHALL, REQUIRED or a definition, `should` for SHOULD or RECOMMENDED, `may` for MAY or OPTIONAL. A quote with no upper-case keyword is read by the same words in any other case, with "can" as a permission. `validate` refuses a level its quote's upper-case keywords disagree with, a stated `should` or `may` its quote does not say, and a citation that leaves the default `must` while its quote says "should", "can" or "may" and no requiring word; a stated `must` records that such a sentence requires in other words. A row whose failing criteria all cite `should` is failed and a warning, and never counts against a capability; a `may` criterion counts like a `must` one (RFC 2119 §5).

development.description: Where the development snapshot states the same requirement in other words. Read under the development specification profile only, in place of `section` and `quote`, and never under the released profile. `validate --profile development` refuses it when its quote does not occur in the snapshot, and when the released quote still occurs there unchanged.

source.description: The snapshot file, relative to the repository root, when it is not the file `source` maps to.

section.description: The element or the section heading in the snapshot, as `section` names one.
The BASE section of its capability folder a document belongs to, by the key `catalogue/chapters.yaml` declares.

context.description: The runtime expression the judged value is read from.
The runtime expression the judged value is read from.

to.description: The document the context must equal: a literal, or a runtime expression.

ignoring.description: RM paths ignored on both sides; `**` matches any depth.

context.description: The runtime expression the judged value is read from.
The runtime expression the judged value is read from.

type.description: The JSON type the context's value must be, one of the six of RFC 8259 §3; an absent value is of no type, and a present `null` is of the type `null`.

oneOf.description: The step's response body validates against the schema its operation declares for the served status and media type. It runs only where a criterion asks for it, and that criterion cites the OAS element.

control.description: The control of a refusal workflow: a `workflowId` of the same document, or `$sourceDescriptions.<name>.<workflowId>` of a `type: arazzo` source, as Arazzo 1.1.0 `dependsOn` names a workflow; a list names one control per arm of an option the refusal runs under. A control is accepted when every row of it passed or failed only criteria that yield a warning, and a refusal row is judged when no listed control that ran was refused and at least one ran.

oneOf.description: A refusal with no twin in the catalogue yet: the open issue in this repository that tracks authoring one. Such a refusal is never judged; every row of it is errored, naming the issue.

principal.description: The principal a step is sent as: `administrative` is a principal the service authorizes for its administrative operations.

scope.description: The scope set of the access token a step presents: an OAuth 2.0 scope value, space-delimited scope tokens in any order (RFC 6749 §3.3), or `$inputs.<name>` to read it from each row. The empty string is a token with no scope.

derive.description: New step outputs by name. Each applies one function of BASE `object_version_id.adoc` to an output the same step declares, whose value has the lexical form `object_id::creating_system_id::version_tree_id`; a value of another form makes the row errored.
